DASCore uses comments for implementation intent, NumPy-style docstrings for API documentation, and `.qmd` pages for guides and examples.

# Comments and docstrings

Comments should explain non-obvious intent, not restate code. Prefer clearer names or smaller functions when comments merely narrate operations.

Use [NumPy-style docstrings](https://numpydoc.readthedocs.io/en/latest/format.html) and accurate type hints. Public objects need complete docstrings; private objects may use a short summary. Describe behavior and constraints, not types already expressed by annotations.

```{python}
from __future__ import annotations

import dascore as dc
from dascore.constants import PatchType


@dc.patch_function()
def add_value(patch: PatchType, value: int | float = 0) -> PatchType:
    """
    Add a scalar to patch data.

    Parameters
    ----------
    patch
        Patch to update.
    value
        Value added to each sample.

    Examples
    --------
    >>> import dascore as dc
    >>> patch = dc.get_example_patch()
    >>> out = add_value(patch, 2)
    >>> assert out.shape == patch.shape
    """
    return patch.new(data=patch.data + value)
```

Docstring examples use [doctest](https://docs.python.org/3/library/doctest.html). Quarto options such as `>>> #| code-fold: true` and headings such as `>>> ### Detail` are preserved in generated API pages.

For IO contracts, document only the formatter's responsibility. `FiberIO.scan()` returns patch-local attrs and a full `CoordManager`; the public scan pipeline adds source path, format, and version. Formats with stored per-sample coordinates return them exactly with `snap=False`.

# Build and test

After the [development install](dev_install.qmd), install [Quarto](https://quarto.org/docs/get-started/) and run:

```bash
python scripts/build_api_docs.py
quarto render dascore/docs
```

Use `quarto preview dascore/docs` for live editing. Generated HTML is under `dascore/docs/_site/`.

Edit `scripts/_templates/_quarto.yml` for navigation; `dascore/docs/_quarto.yml` is generated and overwritten. The API sidebar intentionally lists top-level sections rather than every object; `dascore/docs/api/_metadata.yml` assigns unlisted API pages to it.

The docs build records timing, output size, and URL changes:

```bash
python scripts/_doc_report.py time build_api_docs -- python scripts/build_api_docs.py
python scripts/_doc_report.py index
python scripts/_doc_report.py time quarto_render -- quarto render dascore/docs
python scripts/_doc_report.py site
python scripts/_doc_report.py summary
```

Run these in order. `scripts/_baselines/api_urls.tsv` protects published API URLs; regenerate it with `python scripts/_api_urls.py freeze` only when intentional URL changes are explained in the PR.

A page that is also an agent skill holds only an include; its text, and its executable blocks, live in `dascore/.agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`, so edit that file.

Executable Python blocks in hand-written `.qmd` files, and in the skill files they include, are mirrored into pytest files; blocks with `eval: false` are not tested:

```bash
python scripts/generate_doc_code_tests.py
pytest tests/test_autogenerated_doccode
```

## marimo tutorials

Runnable tutorials become [marimo](https://marimo.io) notebooks that run in the browser; CI builds them, and the `.qmd` files remain the source. Build them before rendering docs locally:

```bash
python -m build --wheel
python scripts/build_notebooks.py
```

This needs `quarto`, `marimo` and `uv` on the path and the generated `_quarto.yml` from `scripts/build_api_docs.py`. It exports the notebooks, with the newest wheel in `dist/` and the example data, to `dascore/docs/marimo/`. The bundled wheel pins notebooks to the documented checkout and avoids WebAssembly-incompatible dependencies of released versions. Rendering without these steps omits the **Open in marimo** links. To try a notebook locally, serve the export (`python -m http.server -d dascore/docs/marimo`) and open a page.

marimo runs cells as a dependency graph, so a tutorial page must define each top-level name, imports included, in only one `{python}` block. Choose a new name rather than reassigning one from an earlier block; names starting with `_` are local to their block and may be reused. The converter would otherwise rename later definitions (`patch_1`) or drop repeated imports, and the notebook would drift from the page, so `tests/test_build_notebooks.py` checks this.

Set `DASCORE_DOC_SITE_URL` for the deployment that notebook links should target. Add tutorial data to `MIRRORED_DATA` in `scripts/build_notebooks.py` to avoid browser downloads and shared-IP rate limits.

# Links, citations, and equations {#cross-references}

Link API objects by placing their import path in backticks:

```markdown
[Patch](`dascore.core.Patch`)
```

From docstrings, link pages relative to `dascore/docs/`, for example `[Documentation](`dascore/docs/contributing/documentation.qmd`)`. In `.qmd` pages, use ordinary relative paths.

Add publications to `dascore/docs/references.bib` and cite them with Pandoc syntax such as `@lindsey2021fiber` or `[@lindsey2021fiber]`.

Use standard LaTeX: `$E=mc^2$` inline or a labeled display for cross-references:

```text
$$
y = mx + b
$$ {#eq-line}

See @eq-line.
```

See the [Quarto documentation](https://quarto.org/docs/) for layout and formatting options.
